records.text: Owens said the veteran traveling with her had served in the U.S. military for 12 years with SEAL Team ONE, had repeatedly been denied a VA appointment, and suffered a seizure one day after arriving in Russia.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

records.text: Owens said the veteran's wife provided evidence that he sought a VA appointment in May and was told his symptoms were psychological and to take Xanax.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And knowing that the VA just kept denying him, his wife sent me all the evidence of that. ... He tried to get an appointment in May. And so to think that this happened, and they kept telling him, no, it's all in your head, he takes some Xanax, is unbelievably frustrating.

records.text: Owens reported that the veteran's wife said removing a brain clot ended his need for a hearing aid, his headaches, and his morning hemoptysis.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: His wife told me that once they removed that clot from his brain, all of the other issues that he was having cleared up. So he, unbeknownst to me, was wearing a hearing aid and now he doesn't need to wear his hearing aid. ... He was having headaches. Now he's not having headaches. He was spitting up blood in the morning.
